newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican protesters strip naked before Congress.
newsitem.headline: Mexican protesters strip naked before Congress.

text.p: A group of about a dozen male protesters stormed the Mexican Congress on Wednesday and stripped naked before legislators in support of a pair of hunger strikers who are near death.
The men entered the legislative chamber in their underwear, paraded onto a stage facing the Congress, turned their behinds to the legislators and dropped their shorts, witnesses said.
The light-hearted touch contrasted to the deadly serious matter of two hunger strikers who are very near death.
The hunger strikers and the strippers are all fired streetsweepers from the Gulf Coast state of Tabasco demanding their jobs back or better severance pay.

The protest supported 300 fired cleaners, who have cast a spotlight on conditions some government workers are forced to endure, as well as Mexico's dire joblessness, embarrasssing the government of President Ernesto Zedillo.
The workers claim they were fired for refusing to perform unpaid, off-duty personal tasks for controversial Tabasco Governor Roberto Madrazo and other officials..

Lying virtually unconscious under a plastic tarpaulin outside the National Human Rights Commission, Jorge Luis Alamilla and Venancio Jimenez could not talk and could barely open their eyes. Reporters on Tuesday were only permitted a brief glimpse of the two men inside their dark shelter.

Concerned doctors, forbidden by the protesters from treating their colleagues, said the two men may have sustained irreversible physical and mental damage from spending almost three months consuming only water, honey and glucose.
Mexican newspapers said the two men could die at any time.
Last weekend, on orders from Zedillo, the Interior Ministry began urgent negotiations to try to end the hunger strike.
It was not immediately clear whether the naked protesters would be charged with any crimes.
